property_summary: Invariant: after any call to Collect(amount) by any user, the contract's MinSum does not change; the mutant removing the nonReentrant_ lock assignment allows a reentrant attacker to change MinSum during Collect, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For all call inputs, calling Collect(...) must NOT change the contract's MinSum (MinSum remains equal before and after Collect); removing the reentrancy lock assignment enables a reentrant attacker to call SetMinSum during Collect and thus change MinSum for some fuzzed inputs.

For every admissible input, calling Collect(...) by any address does not allow an attacker contract used as the recipient of the low-level call to change MinSum during Collect on the correct contract; the mutant that fails to reset the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker (via its fallback/receive) to call SetMinSum during Collect and thus change MinSum for some fuzzed inputs.

For every admissible input, calling Collect(amount) must never change MinSum on the reference contract (MinSum_before == MinSum_after); the mutant that fails to re-set the nonReentrant_ lock can be reentered during Collect allowing a malicious recipient to call SetMinSum and thus change MinSum for some fuzzed inputs.

For every admissible input, if an account with nonzero balance calls Collect(amount) and the low-level send in Collect succeeds to that caller, then MinSum remains unchanged on the reference; the mutant allowing reentrancy (by not re-setting the lock) can be reentered by a malicious recipient during Collect to call SetMinSum and thus change MinSum for some fuzzed inputs.

After one successful call that sets initialized via Initialized(), subsequent call to SetMinSum must revert (i.e., cannot change MinSum) because nonReentrant_ allows only first-time initialization to succeed and further SetMinSum calls revert.
A successful Collect call does not prevent later SetMinSum from being callable (i.e., locked_ is reset), so after Collect one can still call SetMinSum to update MinSum without revert.
After a successful Collect call that returns normally, SetMinSum can still be called successfully (does not revert) and therefore can update MinSum.
After calling Collect, SetMinSum can still be called successfully (does not revert) and thus can update MinSum in the original but not in the mutant that leaves the lock set.
After a normal (non-reverting) call to Collect, subsequent call to SetMinSum does not revert (i.e., remains callable) and thus can update MinSum.

Invariant: after any call to Collect(amount) by any account, the contract's MinSum remains unchanged (reference holds because nonReentrant_ resets the lock allowing SetMinSum to be called later only by initializer flows), but the mutant that leaves locked_ = true can block subsequent SetMinSum calls causing MinSum to differ after interactions — so for some sequence where a caller triggers Collect and then another caller (or same) calls SetMinSum, the reference allows MinSum to be updated while the mutant prevents it.

For any caller, after any sequence where some account first calls Collect(am) and then any account calls SetMinSum(val) (before initialization), the reference contract always allows SetMinSum to update MinSum, but the mutant that leaves locked_ = true can block SetMinSum and therefore may leave MinSum unchanged for some inputs (the test fuzzes caller, am, and newMin to find such a failing case).

For any caller, after calling Collect(amount) (which sets locked_ back to false in the reference), a subsequent call to SetMinSum(newMin) (before Initialized()) must succeed and update MinSum; the mutant that leaves locked_ = true can block SetMinSum causing MinSum not to update for some inputs.

After any successful Collect call by an account, a subsequent SetMinSum call (when contract not initialized) invoked by ANY account must be able to update MinSum in the reference, but the mutant that leaves locked_ stuck true can block SetMinSum causing MinSum to remain unchanged for some fuzzed inputs.

If the contract is not initialized, then after any single call to Collect(...) by some account, a subsequent call to SetMinSum(...) (by any account) must be able to update MinSum; the mutant that leaves the reentrancy lock set true can block SetMinSum and thus violate this rule for some fuzzed inputs.

For all inputs, calling SetMinSum on the reference contract reverts (does not change MinSum) if the contract is already initialized; the mutant removes that guard so for some inputs it will succeed and change MinSum.

For any caller and any value, calling SetMinSum on the correct contract always succeeds (does not revert) and sets MinSum to the provided value; the mutant that leaves the reentrancy lock permanently true causes subsequent SetMinSum calls to revert (fail) for some inputs (e.g., a second SetMinSum call), breaking this rule.

Once Initialized() has been called (intitalized == true), SetLogFile(address) must NOT change the stored Log address; the mutant removes the guard and allows changing Log after initialization, so for some inputs SetLogFile will modify Log in the mutant but not in the reference.

For all inputs, once Initialized() has been called, SetLogFile(address) must NOT change the stored Log address; the mutant (which removes the revert guard) can change Log after initialization for some input address causing a difference.

For all inputs, after Initialized() has been called, calling SetLogFile(...) must NOT change the stored Log address; the mutant removed the revert guard and can change Log after initialization for some input address, violating this invariant.

For all inputs, once Initialized() has been called the stored Log address must remain unchanged by subsequent SetLogFile calls; the mutant (which removes the initialization revert) can change Log for some input address, violating this invariant.

After the contract is Initialized(), calling SetLogFile(address) must not change the stored Log address for any input; the mutant removes the initialization guard and therefore for some addresses SetLogFile will change Log after Initialized(), violating this invariant.

For any caller and any address input, calling SetLogFile(...) on the reference C will set the Log state variable to the provided address iff the contract is not yet initialized (intitalized == false); the mutant inverts the check and thus may fail to set Log when intitalized is false (so there exist inputs where after SetLogFile the reference has Log == _log but the mutant retains a different Log).

For any address input _log and any call context, the reference C always sets its public Log to _log after calling SetLogFile(_log) when intitalized is false; the mutant can fail to set Log (it only assigns when intitalized is true) so there exist inputs where after SetLogFile the reference's Log equals the provided address but the mutant's Log does not.

If the contract is not initialized, calling SetLogFile(_log) always sets the public Log to _log; the mutant inverts the check and may leave Log unchanged for some _log and initialization state, so there exist inputs where reference sets Log but mutant does not.

If the contract is not initialized, calling SetLogFile(_log) always updates the public Log variable to _log; the mutant inverts the check and may leave Log unchanged for some _log, so there exist inputs where reference sets Log but mutant does not.

If the contract is not yet initialized, calling SetLogFile(_log) on the reference always sets the public Log to _log; the mutant inverts the check and therefore for some _log calls it will fail to set Log (leaving it unchanged).
For any caller, after calling Initialized() the contract's public boolean `intitalized` becomes true (reference); the mutant flips it to false, so some calls leave `intitalized` != true.
After any call to Initialized() by any caller, the public boolean intitalized must be true; the mutant that sets it to false causes this assertion to fail for some inputs (some caller addresses).

For every caller and input, calling C.Initialized() sets the public boolean intitalized to true (reference); the mutant that sets it to false breaks this property for callers (some fuzzed caller addresses) because the stored flag differs after the call.

For every caller address, after calling C.Initialized() the public boolean intitalized becomes true; the mutant that sets it to false violates this by leaving intitalized == false for at least some caller addresses.

For every address that calls C.Initialized(), the contract's public bool intitalized becomes true (reference); the mutant that sets it to false violates this because after the call intitalized can be false for some caller addresses.
